proposed.def: The separate high-smoothness empirical higher-order SCoDiTE estimator and oracle-calibrated test.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The high-smoothness construction must have its own symbol so that the existing collision and occupancy handle remains available in the rough regime.
This adds the explicit sample map requested for the high-smoothness theorem without replacing the low-smoothness collision and occupancy construction.

proposed.justification: The theorem isolates a separate high-smoothness empirical higher-order construction and proves its uniform Hilbert-risk bound, while the constant-contrast path supplies only the conditional parametric converse.
proposed.gap: Liu, Mukherjee, Newey, and Robins prove scalar empirical higher-order efficiency results; they do not provide this Hilbert-valued common-anchor correction, its exact product-residual identity, or the resulting uniform SCoDiTE test.
proposed.consumer: For total nuisance smoothness above the elbow, the result supplies an oracle-calibrated, density-robust root-rate SCoDiTE test; the rough collision and occupancy analysis remains a distinct downstream problem.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The theorem must consume only the new high-smoothness handle. Removing its former dependency on the rough collision handle preserves all low-smoothness inbound edges and clears the obsolete upper-bound obligation.

prose_updates.tldr: The all-tests SCoDiTE problem has two mathematically separate branches. When \(t>d/2\), a cell-local polynomial empirical higher-order estimator with rank \(M\asymp n^\gamma=o(n)\), a finite Neumann correction, and a common \(K_X\)-anchor has uniform mean-squared error \(O(n^{-1})\) over every bounded positive design density, without smoothness of \(f_X\) or of the feature map. Its deterministic class-oracle variance envelope gives uniform size and root-rate power; a regular constant-contrast path gives the matching lower bound when that path belongs to the class. For \(0<t\le d/2\), the separate collision and occupancy handle remains unchanged: the legal fuzzy construction proves the slower uniform-design lower radius \(n^{-2t/(2t+d)}\) for \(0<s\le1/2\), while the arbitrary-density match, spectral method classification, and adaptive grid remain open. Characteristicness of the outcome kernel does not turn the covariate-smoothed null into pointwise conditional homogeneity.

project_justification.gap: Existing SCoDiTE theory is first order and pointwise in the law, direct spectral tests omit causal nuisances, and scalar empirical higher-order results do not establish a Hilbert-valued common-anchor expansion or a uniform SCoDiTE test. Below the smoothness elbow, no checked result matches the legal fuzzy lower experiment under an arbitrary bounded design density.
project_justification.niche: The paper separates a proved density-robust high-smoothness root-rate theorem from the answer-open rough-design all-tests modulus, then asks when identity or resolvent spectral weighting attains that modulus.
project_justification.fill: Above the elbow, a separate explicit higher-order construction uses cell-local polynomial spans, stabilized arm Gram matrices, finite Neumann chains, and two one-sided plus one common-anchor correction. Their exact inclusion--exclusion identity leaves the product of the propensity and arm-embedding projection residuals while evaluating \(K_X\) exactly, which yields uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) Hilbert risk and oracle-calibrated testing. The original collision and occupancy handle is retained only for the rough branch, where the paired exact-null tables and fuzzy lower bound feed the unresolved arbitrary-density frontier and its spectral and adaptive consumers.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For \(t>d/2\), the explicit construction uses no preliminary nuisance fit: it estimates arm Gram matrices on deterministic half-samples and applies finite ordered higher-order corrections on the opposite halves. For \(0<t\le d/2\), the distinct block-local collision and occupancy handle remains the proposed route; Wald comparisons additionally require a cross-fitted covariance estimate.

prose_updates.related_work: Jain and Luedtke (2026) define the SCoDiTE moment, its efficient Hilbert influence function, and fixed-operator MMD and Wald tests; their first-order product-rate theory does not supply the higher-order uniform test proved here. Liu, Mukherjee, Newey, and Robins (2026, arXiv:1705.07577v5) prove semiparametric efficiency without density smoothness for scalar missing-at-random and doubly robust functionals using empirical Gram bases with rank \(o(n)\). The high-smoothness theorem adapts that architecture through an explicit common-anchor inclusion--exclusion correction and proves its risk directly; it does not import a scalar theorem. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) motivate the localized fuzzy-hypothesis architecture in the separate rough branch, whose nonfactorizing alternative table is specific to the SCoDiTE null. Hagrass, Sriperumbudur, and Li (2024) and Balasubramanian, Li, and Yuan (2021) provide direct-sample spectral arguments under different metrics, while Schrab et al. (2023) provide an aggregation template. None resolves the rough arbitrary-density SCoDiTE modulus or the requested spectral iff and adaptive-grid results.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The high-smoothness test is calibrated by the deterministic envelope \(V_\star\), whose finiteness is proved uniformly but whose numerical value is a class-oracle constant rather than a data-derived critical value. This suffices for the minimax existence and size theorem but is not yet a practical calibration recipe. In the early-kill rough case \(d=1\) and \(\beta_e=\beta_m=0.2\), the nominal uniform-design partition has \(K_h\asymp n^{10/9}>n\), outside both the proved high-smoothness construction and the scalar empirical-HOIF regime. The remaining audit is therefore still the rough arbitrary-density upper procedure and its match to a primitive occupancy functional. The two-outcome family is only a least-favorable proof device; an attaining rough procedure must handle the multivariate wealth outcome.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The density-robust root-rate upper theorem is proved for \(t>d/2\) by an explicit finite-order Hilbert-valued estimator with \(M=o(n)\). Its matching root-rate lower bound, and hence equality, is conditional on the stated nondegenerate quadratic-mean differentiable constant-contrast path. The calibration envelope is deterministic and finite but oracle. The known-propensity benchmark, corrected rough uniform-design fuzzy lower branch, and Fourier quotient-null result remain separate established or posed components. For \(0<t\le d/2\), the collision and occupancy handle has not been replaced: the arbitrary-density equivalence, the spectral iff classification, and the adaptive regularization grid remain open. No claim is made that \(K_h>n\) itself proves an occupancy penalty or that characteristic constituent kernels make the smoothed null identical to conditional homogeneity.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem now has a separate explicit estimator, an exact product-residual identity, uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) Hilbert risk, finite oracle calibration, and a conditional local-path converse.
statement_notes.gap: Scalar empirical higher-order efficiency theorems do not establish the common-anchor Hilbert correction or this uniform testing guarantee.
statement_notes.consumer: Above the smoothness elbow, the 401(k) analysis has a mathematically size-valid oracle threshold; practical estimation of that threshold and the rough-design frontier remain separate tasks.
